aiAgentFacts.fact: In a 2023 bilingual global survey with 1,262 completed responses from 66 countries, cat caregivers' Feline Grimace Scale scores were not significantly different from veterinarians' scores of the same images, except for muzzle tension.
The single-rater intraclass correlation for caregivers' total Feline Grimace Scale score was 0.65, which the study classified as good reliability.
Orbital tightening (ICCsingle 0.69) and ear position (0.65) were the most reliable action units among caregivers; whiskers change (0.37) and head position (0.38) were the least reliable.
Caregivers scored muzzle tension significantly higher than veterinarians did (0.9 vs 0.7, P=0.035) — the only action unit showing a significant group difference.
Demographic variables did not significantly affect the Feline Grimace Scale scores caregivers assigned.
The Feline Grimace Scale comprises five action units scored 0–2 each: ear position, orbital tightening, muzzle tension, whiskers change, and head position.
This survey assessed acute pain only; its findings do not extend to chronic or slowly progressive pain in cats.
Participants scored 10 static photographic images, not live cats; the study measured inter-rater agreement, not any clinical or welfare outcome of owner-performed scoring.

historyQuestions: Not prescribed by this paper. Its action units (ear position, orbital tightening, muzzle tension, whiskers change, head position) indicate which facial features carry the most reliable signal, but the study does not specify owner-facing history questions.
redFlags: Not addressed — this study does not identify red-flag findings warranting urgent referral, and defines no owner-facing action threshold.
differentialDiagnosesMentioned: Not addressed — the study measures rater agreement on a pain scale, not the cause of pain.
recommendedDiagnosticWorkups: Not addressed — no diagnostic workup is evaluated or recommended by this study.
urgentCareTriggers: Not addressed by this paper. Suspected pain remains a reason to contact a veterinarian; this study provides no threshold that would justify home observation instead.

limitations: Author-acknowledged: convenience sampling recruited largely through a cat-welfare organization — participants are unusually engaged and not representative of cat owners generally
Author-acknowledged: 86% of respondents identified as female; male raters were underrepresented
Design-level: raters scored 10 static images rather than live cats, removing movement, lighting, angle, and observer-presence effects present in real use
Design-level: the study measures inter-rater agreement only — no clinical, welfare, or decision-quality outcome of owner scoring was assessed
Scope: acute pain only; the instrument was neither designed nor tested here for chronic pain
Two of the five action units (whiskers change, head position) reached only 'reasonable' reliability among caregivers, so the total score is not uniformly reliable across its components
